finding.claim: POST /settings/email is decorated with @login_optional instead of @login_required, so unauthenticated requests reach the email-change operation with g.uid = None. The handler never checks g.uid. Depending on set_email's handling of a None uid, an anonymous attacker could change an account email (for example a row matched on a NULL or empty uid, or a fallback or default account), which enables account takeover through password reset. At minimum it is a broken authentication gate on a sensitive state-changing endpoint, and it is inconsistent with /settings/password, which uses @login_required.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP POST to /settings/email with no session cookie
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37, which changes the account email, a protected operation

trace.note: @login_optional applied, so there is no authentication enforcement
g.uid = session.get('uid') evaluates to None for anonymous callers and the request continues
set_email(None, ...) is called with no check that g.uid is set
set_email is a stub here, so the real impact depends on its implementation

finding.guards_checked: Checked for login_required (absent on this route; present on /settings/password at line 42), any in-handler check of g.uid (none), and any CSRF protection (none). The route is Flask public ingress, with no internal-only binding. set_email is a stub, so the exploitability of a None uid is unverified and the severity is capped accordingly. Not reported as separate findings: no app.secret_key is set in this file (likely configured elsewhere), and the new email and password values are hardcoded placeholders (stub code).

verdict.reason: routes.py:35 applies @login_optional (which sets g.uid=None for anonymous callers at routes.py:22 and never aborts), and change_email at routes.py:37 calls set_email(g.uid, ...) with no check, unlike /settings/password at routes.py:42, which uses @login_required; set_email is a stub (routes.py:48), so the impact depends on its real implementation, but the missing auth gate on a state-changing endpoint is real.
